items.title: Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability (Broccoli2Shell)
items.summary: An unchecked return value vulnerability in Google Brotli, a dependency used by Adobe Commerce, could allow remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory, disclose sensitive contents, cause DoS, or execute arbitrary code. This vulnerability was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on October 27, 2026, indicating active exploitation.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Unrestricted File Upload (PolyShell)
items.summary: An unrestricted upload of a file with a dangerous type in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source can lead to arbitrary code execution. This vulnerability, known as PolyShell, was fixed in APSB26-73 (July 14, 2026) but was added to CISA's KEV catalog on October 27, 2026, due to active exploitation.

items.title: Security Update for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This security bulletin addresses multiple critical and important vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce, Magento Open Source, and Adobe Commerce B2B. Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, arbitrary file system write, and security feature bypass.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Remote Code Execution (BlockStrap)
items.summary: BlockStrap is a CVSS 10.0 vulnerability in Magento and Adobe Commerce that allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution via a template engine injection. Adobe fixed this flaw in APSB26-153, but new installations may still require a manual patch.

items.title: Emergency Security Hotfix for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This emergency hotfix addresses CVE-2026-75650, a critical vulnerability in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution and was actively exploited as a zero-day.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Zero-Day Remote Code Execution (StyleSmuggler)
items.summary: Sansec discovered StyleSmuggler, a Magento and Adobe Commerce zero-day vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers remote code execution, with attacks starting on September 4, 2026. Adobe released an emergency hotfix (APSB26-146) on September 7, 2026, for this CVSS 10.0 flaw.

items.title: Security Update Available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: This security update resolves critical and high-severity vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce, Magento Open Source, and Adobe Commerce B2B. The most critical issue, CVE-2026-71362, allows unauthenticated privilege escalation and was actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: Adobe Commerce Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
items.summary: A critical incorrect authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce (CVSS 9.1) could be leveraged by an unauthenticated attacker to gain elevated access to sensitive resources and hijack customer accounts. Adobe addressed this vulnerability in APSB26-92 and noted active exploitation attempts.

items.title: Security Update Available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: This security update for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source addresses multiple vulnerabilities, including critical ones that could lead to arbitrary code execution. It includes the fix for CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), which was later found to be actively exploited.
